newsitem.title: USA: WTO rules against U.S. on Costa Rican underwear.
newsitem.headline: WTO rules against U.S. on Costa Rican underwear.

text.p: A World Trade Organization dispute settlement panel ruled against a U.S. program restricting underwear imports from Costa Rica, the U.S. Trade Representative's Office (USTR) said on Friday.
The panel urged the United States to end limits on the imports, but the USTR said there were aspects of the ruling that were in the United States' favor.

The USTR cited a panel finding it said preserved the U.S. ability to take safeguard action on re-import trade and U.S. flexibility in providing favorable treatment to that trade in accordance with the rules of the WTO textile agreement.

In a statement, Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said the United States believes the restrictions on Costa Rican underwear imports were consistent with the rules of the WTO textile and clothing agreement.

"During the next few weeks, we will evaluate the report carefully, in light of our objectives for the U.S. textile program and in consultation with our industry and with Congress," Barshefsky said. Under WTO rules, the United States may appeal the settlement panel's decision.
